claims.text: Ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder initially consists of a metastable BCC solid solution with high defect density.
The initial ball-milled powder may contain oxygen contamination.
SPS at 900–980 °C for 10–15 minutes under 30–50 MPa in argon is a suitable processing window for this alloy.
At 900–980 °C, enhanced atomic diffusion enables Ti and V segregation to grain boundaries.
Segregated Ti and V nucleate a nanoscale Ti/V-rich BCC intermetallic phase, potentially Ti2Fe or a V-rich solid solution.
The Ti/V-rich secondary phase forms a percolating network at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary secondary-phase network acts as a diffusion barrier that suppresses magnesium evaporation.
The secondary-phase network limits oxygen ingress.
The Ti/V-rich phase pins grain boundaries and retards coarsening of the BCC matrix.
Precipitation of the secondary phase increases hardness through precipitation strengthening.
Suppressing magnesium loss and pore growth increases the relative density of the sintered alloy.
A continuous Ti/V-rich barrier network enhances oxidation and corrosion resistance.
Below 800 °C, insufficient atomic mobility prevents adequate nucleation and growth of the barrier phase and causes incomplete densification.
Above 1000 °C, excessive magnesium evaporation and rapid grain growth cause composition deviation and disrupt the barrier network.
Sintering times shorter than five minutes are insufficient to precipitate the proposed barrier phase.
Processing in the proposed temperature window will produce greater than 98% relative density.
Processing in the proposed temperature window will produce Vickers hardness above 400 HV.
Processing in the proposed temperature window will reduce oxidation rate by 50% relative to samples sintered at 800 °C or 1000 °C.
The passive film will have an outer MgO/Al2O3 layer and an inner Ti/V-rich diffusion-barrier layer.

A diffusion-controlled mechanism would give the 950 °C sample the lowest oxidation rate and a continuous Ti/V-rich film layer, whereas a surface-reaction-limited mechanism would give similar rates across sintering temperatures and no distinct barrier layer.

contradictions.description: The proposed secondary phase is called an intermetallic while a V-rich solid solution is simultaneously offered as an example; a solid solution and an intermetallic are distinct phase categories.
